clue.text: Pursuit of rolling credit acquires personal new crockery

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
your own things are personal to you
green means new or inexperienced
bowls are items of crockery

explanation.surface: Someone paying on credit picks up a new set of their own dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown green bowls is a form of the lawn game played on a green with a raised centre, popular in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowls is a sport in which players roll weighted balls towards a jack, so it is a pastime built on rolling.

clue.text: Ready meals can cook over counter

parts.note: a can is slang for a toilet, and a public toilet is a convenience in British English

indicators.note: counter means running against, so the two short words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
of can mean concerning, like over in 'fight over' and 'think of'

explanation.surface: Instructions on a packet of ready meals: you can heat them up over a kitchen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a kitchen worktop but is the reversal signal. In British English a public toilet is a convenience, and 'can' is slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-prepared dishes that need only heating are called convenience food, the same thing as ready meals.

clue.text: Wild dog chasing its tail, it seems

indicators.note: the dog chases its tail when its head letter runs round to follow behind the rest

parts.note: a corgi is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A frantic dog spinning round after its own tail seems to have gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The C at the front of CORGI moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgic is a rare adjective meaning orgiastic, frenzied and unrestrained, hence wild.

clue.text: Brainbox, or fruitcake?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: the case holding the nut, slang for the head, so a skull
second meaning: fruitcake is slang for a crazy person

explanation.walkthrough: Brainbox usually means a clever person; here it is read literally as the box round the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is informally a lunatic, the same as a fruitcake, and literally a case for the nut or head.

clue.text: I'm not sure about solitary chap who's refined substance in lab

indicators.note: about means turned round here, so the hesitation sound is read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound made when hesitating or unsure
a means one, single
a gent is a gentleman, a refined chap

explanation.surface: Someone is hesitant about a lonely, cultured man who refines things in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ER into RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a chemical used in laboratory reactions, a substance used in tests and analysis.

clue.text: Consecutive characters written on top of the tin?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part is written on top of the second

parts.note: the letters L, M and N follow one another in the alphabet, spelt out as el, em, en

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A label: a run of letters printed on the lid of a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter names EL EM EN sit above T, the first letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is a chemical element, symbol Sn, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Traditional Italian goods record incorporated mixed meat produce

indicators.note: incorporated means taken into the body of something, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: bona is Latin, the traditional language of Italy, for goods or property
a log is a record, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: Classic Italian products, documented as including assorted processed meats.
explanation.walkthrough: Traditional Italian is Latin here, not modern Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a large smoked sausage made from a mixture of meats, named after the city.

clue.text: SOS issued by nervous Osmosis in your compiling team is annoying

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other phrase

parts.note: a setter calls himself and his colleagues we, so 'your compiling team is' becomes we are

indicators.note: nervous means jittery and unsettled, so the letters are shaken up
SOS issued by the word means those letters come out of it

explanation.surface: A jittery member of the setting team called Osmosis sends out distress calls, which is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Osmosis poses as a setter's pseudonym. Removing the letters of SOS leaves M, O, I, S to be jumbled; the setter speaking of himself and colleagues as 'we' supplies the outer phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome is tiresome and tedious, the same as annoying or irksome.

clue.text: PTO for punchlines

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells the reader to look at the other side of the page, and that is where the jokes are

explanation.walkthrough: On a joke card the punchline is printed on the back, so PTO sends you to the side with the funny part.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means to find humour in a bad situation; here it literally means look at the page's amusing reverse.

clue.text: "Incubus" is the dark horse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an incubus is an oppressive bad dream or burden
second meaning, read literally: a mare of the night

explanation.walkthrough: A dark horse is normally an unexpected contender; here it is split into night (dark) and mare (horse).
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a demon once believed to cause bad dreams, and the word also means a nightmare itself.

clue.text: What comes in handy for butcher's unlimited holidays

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.words: What comes in handy for butcher's
parts.note: a cleaver is a butcher's chopping tool

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop worker gets endless holiday time.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off work granted to an employee, as in annual leave, so it covers holidays.

clue.text: Husband's off from here with ladies, say, in Vatican City?

indicators.note: in puts the toilet inside the shortened word
Husband's off means the husband's letter is removed

parts.note: hence means from this place
H is the abbreviation for husband
the ladies is a women's toilet, and lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: A husband leaves with women and visits the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ladies' is the British name for a women's public toilet, hence a lav.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatican City is a tiny state wholly surrounded by Rome, a classic example of a territory enclosed within another.

clue.text: People from Cornwall, perhaps controversially, single out emmets from Hants

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
from signals taking the insects away from the county name

parts.note: taken as written
emmet is a dialect word for an ant

explanation.surface: Cornish people single out tourists from Hampshire, a touchy matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county; emmets is also Cornish slang for tourists, which suits the surface. Cornwall is part of England, though some Cornish dispute being called English.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornish people are English by nationality, though some in Cornwall see themselves as a separate Celtic nation.

clue.text: Mum's mum, in and out of India, died

indicators.note: out of means these letters leave the phrase

parts.note: the letters of these two words, read as one string; that the answer also runs across them unchanged is a coincidence, since the clue names India and died as the letters to drop
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grandmother who came and went from India before she died.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and D out of the letters of 'in and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is a familiar British word for a grandmother, here the mother of one's mother.

clue.text: Vary the tone of pub spotted in report

indicators.note: in report means as heard spoken, so the phrase sounds like the answer

parts.note: inn is a pub and flecked means spotted

explanation.surface: Change your voice when talking about a pub seen in a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflect the voice is to modulate its pitch or intonation, changing how it sounds.

clue.text: The point of an index?

parts.note: the index finger ends in a point, its tip

explanation.walkthrough: An index sounds like a book's list of contents; it is the forefinger.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of the forefinger is literally the point of the index finger.

clue.text: With regular absences from school, pass

indicators.note: regular absences mean every other letter is missing, leaving alternate letters

explanation.surface: A pupil who skips school regularly still passes.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a mountain pass, the lowest point of a ridge between two peaks.

clue.text: Separate fine for a strange visitor from the East

indicators.note: in an across answer reading from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
ET is the alien visitor from the film

explanation.surface: An alien from the Orient is fined and kept apart.
explanation.walkthrough: F + FOR A + ET read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear off is to separate a piece by ripping it away, as with a tear-off slip.

clue.text: One year they expect to retain more than one such private investigator

indicators.text: to retain more than one such
indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them, and they do so more than once: in both 'One year' and 'they expect'

explanation.surface: Detectives are hired every year to keep watch on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides in 'onE YEar' and again in 'thEY Expect'; either will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A private eye is a private detective, so the shortened form stands for one.

clue.text: Nine-piece, unfashionable backing group of the 70s

parts.note: non-U means not upper-class, socially unacceptable

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the band's initials are read in reverse

parts.note: ELP, Emerson, Lake and Palmer, was a 1970s rock group

explanation.surface: An uncool nonet plays backing for a seventies band.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U was a 1950s British label for speech and habits judged not upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonuple means ninefold or made of nine parts, so a nine-piece set.

clue.text: Inverted spear I put through just over three dumplings

indicators.note: put through means pushed into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: pi is about 3.14, just over three

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, so in a down answer the letters run the other way

parts.note: to gore is to pierce or spear with a horn

explanation.surface: A spear turned upside down pierces three-and-a-bit dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just over three' is the number pi, about 3.14, not a count of dumplings; 'spear' is the verb, as a bull spears with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierogi are filled Polish dumplings, usually boiled and sometimes fried.

clue.text: Designate institution occupying Burlington House complex?

parts.note: elect, after a title, means chosen but not yet in office, like designate
the Royal Academy of Arts is based at Burlington House in Piccadilly, London

explanation.surface: Naming a body housed in a London building as complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Complex is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electra complex is a psychoanalytic term for a daughter's attachment to her father, so it is one kind of complex.

clue.text: Intermediate to put down stake, then go north

parts.note: to bet is to stake money
go is slang for urinate, and so is wee

explanation.surface: A gambler places a stake and then heads north, in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Between describes something in the middle, positioned in the gap separating two things.

clue.text: Output from sugar-making station includes CO2?

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a base is a station, as in a military base
carbon dioxide is an example of a gas

explanation.surface: A sugar factory's emissions contain carbon dioxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagasse is the fibrous residue left after sugar cane is crushed, a by-product of sugar production.

clue.text: Nothing excited historian, so given marching orders

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
given marching orders means dismissed, so the letters of 'so' are taken out

explanation.surface: A worked-up historian was sacked for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S and O from HISTORIAN and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin air means nothingness, as when something vanishes into thin air or appears out of it.

clue.text: Arable area, in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the words is used, the answer sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A section of farmland that can be ploughed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a meadow or a stretch of open ground, often land that is or was under the plough.

clue.text: Partner who was, for one summer, French interpreter

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
eg means for example, for one
été is French for summer

explanation.surface: A former lover who once spent a summer translating French.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegete explains and expounds texts, especially scripture, so is an interpreter of them.

clue.text: Challenge earns favourable vote

parts.note: to earn is to gain
ay, or aye, is a vote in favour

explanation.surface: A motion is challenged but wins a vote in its favour.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, so to challenge a statement.

clue.text: Went up a long way — and came down fast!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., past of sky, is to hit a ball high into the air
second meaning: ..., past of ski, is to go down a slope on skis

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings come from two different verbs, sky and ski, that share one past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket ball that was skied soared upward, while a skier who skied sped downhill on snow.

clue.text: Could this be barbecue paste?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to paste is slang for to thrash, so to beat or surpass

explanation.walkthrough: Paste looks like a food spread for the barbecue; it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or beat them, and a barbecue is literally a do held out of doors.

clue.text: One has concealed message about boozer for returning maestro

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the pieces read right to left

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nina is a hidden message in a crossword grid
C, short for circa, means about
a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A conductor has hidden a note about a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer looks like a pub; it is the drinker. I + NINA + C + SOT read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian conductor, a maestro of the orchestra.

clue.text: In which your partner's double crossing?

parts.note: a duplicate is a double, an exact copy
a bridge is a crossing over a river or road

explanation.surface: Your partner is betraying you, a double-cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double crossing' reads as treachery but is split into two synonyms; the definition describes a card game played in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicate bridge is a tournament form of the partnership card game in which identical hands are replayed at different tables.
